paper_metadata.title: Quantum Machine Learning for Credit Scoring

summary: The paper studies a hybrid quantum-classical FULL HYBRID (FH) credit-scoring classifier on a Singapore SME dataset using PennyLane simulators, with 6-18 qubits tested for model scaling and up to 20 qubits for timing. The FH model achieved AUC 0.75 versus 0.73 for the best classical model at 350 epochs, but the classical model also reached AUC 0.75 when trained longer (3500-5000 epochs), so no practical quantum advantage is demonstrated.

experiments.description: Hybrid classical-quantum neural network (FH:NN/VC-DRC) for SME credit scoring on a Singapore dataset, evaluated against classical neural-network baselines while varying qubit count and number of data-reuploading blocks on a PennyLane simulator.

algorithm.ansatz: variational quantum circuit with angle embedding, parameterized rotation gates, and CNOT entangling layers; data re-uploading via repeated VC blocks
algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained for 350 epochs; classical counterpart also compared at up to 3500/5000 epochs; overfitting observed on average after 350 epochs

problem_formulation.encoding_details: classical features encoded into qubits using Rx angle embedding; higher-dimensional inputs padded and split across qubits as needed
problem_formulation.objective_function: binary classification of SME credit default vs non-default, optimized via binary cross-entropy and ROC/AUC
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: dropout regularization in classical layers; no explicit quantum constraint handling reported

problem_instance.description: Binary SME credit scoring for Singapore companies using accounting, operating, geo-sociological, and incorporation data

dataset_specification.description: ~2,300 SME firms incorporated over 1940-2016; 246 class-1 (default/unhealthy) companies and 2000 class-0 companies sampled; 24 primary features available, maximum 21 used in experiments; split into 1798 training rows, 180 validation rows, 270 test rows

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: standard pipeline plus proprietary processing; same preprocessing as best XGBoost classical model; angle embedding with Rx; dropout added after classical layers
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: average ROC/AUC over 5 simulations for each configuration; train/validation/test split fixed across runs

implementation_details.classical_solver: SGD-trained classical neural network; classical baselines include linear regression, logistic regression, support vector machines, random forest, and best classical model/XGBoost
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: ROC/AUC evaluation and comparison to classical baselines

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: overfitting observed on average after 350 epochs; FH reached comparable AUC with fewer epochs than classical model

speedup_claims.conditions: FH model trained for 350 epochs versus classical model trained for 3500 epochs for comparable prediction performance
speedup_claims.caveats: Classical model could reach the same AUC of 0.75 when trained longer; this is a training-efficiency comparison, not a proven computational speedup.

speedup_claims.conditions: FH model trained for 350 epochs versus classical model trained for 5000 epochs to reach the highest reported classical score
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper notes the classical model improved with more epochs; the comparison is not necessarily apples-to-apples because the stopping criteria differ.

speedup_claims.conditions: using IBM Qiskit Runtime to run classical and quantum code as one unit
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a cited platform capability, not an experiment result from this paper.

complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: 629,300 circuit executions for 350 epochs and 1798 training samples

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: No demonstrated crossover; quantum model matches classical at AUC 0.75 only after the classical model is trained longer (3500-5000 epochs).
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require a real QPU with substantially lower circuit-evaluation overhead and better scaling than the simulator; however, the paper provides no evidence of a practical resource advantage.
limiting_factors: No demonstrated improvement over the best classical model at equal or comparable training budget
Classical model reaches the same AUC of 0.75 when trained longer
Large circuit-execution count (629,300 executions for 350 epochs and 1798 training samples)
Scaling overhead with qubit count and number of blocks

notes: Hardware is reported as PennyLane emulator/simulator; no real QPU used.

The paper reports scaling experiments over 6-18 qubits and up to 20 qubits for timing, but does not specify a single fixed qubit count for the main experiment, so num_qubits is left null and the range is captured in hyperparameters.
No explicit circuit depth, gate counts, shot count, or variational parameter count are reported.
The paper explicitly states no quantum computer noise was introduced because simulators were used.
Classical baselines are included only as comparison, not separate quantum experiments.
The paper reports AUC 0.75 for the FH model and AUC 0.73 for the best classical model at 350 epochs, but also reports the classical model reaches 0.75 when trained to 5000 epochs.
This supports parity at best, not a demonstrated quantum advantage.
